location: Intent > Approach (authority) vs SPEC.md > Constraints (cleanup sentence)
issue: The decided cleanup placement was written back to cell-contract.md only (Config keys > psm_e2e_slots: 'Inside wait-slots, before its first count'; Docs to update: 'in wait-slots'). SPEC.md > Constraints still says ps-run-layer runs --cleanup-orphans 'automatically before waiting for slots in every mode'. SPEC.md calls itself the canonical, preservation-validated contract, so the two authoritative files now give opposite orders, and this slice spec cites only cell-contract.md.
implementation_impact: A reviewer or a later bmad-spec validation that reads the kernel will flag the implemented order (wait-slots opens first, then cleanup) as nonconforming. The CAP-1 slice, whose docs are built on this one, may copy the stale wording into SKILL.md or headless.md.
suggestion: Amend SPEC.md > Constraints to match cell-contract.md ('runs automatically inside wait-slots, before its first slot count, in every mode'). Name SPEC.md in this spec's write-back note so both files change in the same commit.

location: Design Notes > Admission ('Before the first pass ps-run-layer truncates every queued version's progress log ...') vs Runner > Output (docker_available() skip)
issue: The spec orders truncation, then wait-slots START, then cleanup, then the first count. It never places the existing docker_available() skip check in that sequence. The contract only says the skip happens 'before slot counting', and wait-slots now opens before slot counting. If truncation and the wait-slots START happen first, a Docker-absent run wipes every version's previous progress log. It also leaves a wait-slots phase whose outcome is none of ok/no-slots/cancelled/stopped. The DONE rule then writes 'DONE rc=0' (the run exit code) into logs of versions that never ran.
implementation_impact: Either order passes the listed tests, because no I/O row covers Docker being absent. One choice destroys the last useful logs on every skipped run and writes misleading DONE lines. It also needs a wait-slots outcome the spec does not define.
suggestion: State that the docker_available() skip check runs before any progress log is truncated, before any wait-slots opens and before cleanup, so a skipped run touches no progress log. Add an I/O row: docker absent → 'skipped', exit 0, nothing appended, existing logs unchanged.

location: Boundaries > Always > Child ('--sequential-browsers ... every _new_cell key null ...') + Design Notes > Records
issue: A child not-run cell has started_at/finished_at null, so build_record fills started_at with ps-run-layer's admission time and finished_at with the record write time. For a Firefox cell left not-run after Chromium failed, wall_clock therefore covers pull, bring-up, install, the whole Chromium drive and teardown. The decision not to start the engine was made by the child, mid-run, not at admission. The contract field rule ('when ps-run-layer admitted it or decided not to start it') does not fit this case.
implementation_impact: Each e2e_cells entry for a not-run engine shows a wall_clock of many minutes for a cell that never ran. That data feeds the CAP-6 boot-vs-browser analysis and the SPEC's before/after timing report, and it tells the operator the wrong thing about where time went.
suggestion: Have the child set started_at = finished_at = utc_now() at the moment it decides not to start the engine (an exception to 'every _new_cell key null'), so wall_clock is about 0. As an alternative, ps-run-layer can set both fields to the write time for a child not-run cell. Add the case to the Sequential child test.

location: Tasks > docs (file list) vs references/e2e-quickstart.md and SKILL.md Lapis 4 direct runs
issue: A direct ps-e2e-run.py run now always stamps psm.slots=1 and so uses one slot of the shared daemon-wide cap. It never goes through admission, though: it does not wait in wait-slots and does not respect psm_e2e_slots. The quickstart TDD loop (e2e-quickstart.md lines 43, 72, 149, 160) runs exactly this. The docs task updates SKILL.md, run-phases.md, headless.md, the interim companion and README, but not e2e-quickstart.md, and none of them warns about this.
implementation_impact: An operator running the quickstart loop while another session runs a ps-run-layer gate can fill the cap without knowing it. The other session's queued cells then hit no-slots after the startup timeout (inconclusive, infra retry), and nothing in the docs explains why. The cap can also be overshot, because direct runs never check it.
suggestion: Add references/e2e-quickstart.md (and the direct-run sentence in SKILL.md Lapis 4) to the docs task. Say that direct runs are counted against psm_e2e_slots but bypass admission, so they can push other sessions into no-slots, and recommend ps-run-layer --cells when the daemon is shared.

location: Design Notes > Admission ('ALIVE detail first count pending until the first count') + Records ('every record of a spawned version gets that entry merged')
issue: The cleanup routine runs inside the open wait-slots phases, so every version's wait-slots duration includes cleanup time. That is up to 60 s for each of the two listings plus up to 60 s per orphan removed. A run that never waited for a slot still records a large wait-slots value in every cell's phase_durations. During cleanup the ALIVE detail reads 'first count pending', which tells the operator nothing about the cleanup.
implementation_impact: CAP-6 timings and the SPEC's mandatory before/after report count orphan cleanup as slot contention, so an operator can lower psm_e2e_slots or blame other sessions when the time actually went to removing dead containers. During a long cleanup the progress log cannot be told apart from a stuck first count.
suggestion: Keep the decided placement, and make the time visible. Set the ALIVE detail to 'cleanup-orphans running' while the routine runs and to 'first count pending' only after it ends. Include the cleanup seconds in its stderr summary. State in run-phases.md that wait-slots includes the automatic cleanup.

location: Boundaries > Always > Child ('The child judges an engine's fail with cell_state ...') vs ps-e2e-run.py _plan_layers()/cell_state
issue: cell_state loads ps-plan-layers lazily (_plan_layers). Today that load happens only in exit_code(), after output is written. Engine fail-fast moves it into the engine loop, after bring-up, install and the first engine's drive. ps-plan-layers itself loads ps-static-scan and a second copy of ps-flashlight-run, calling sys.exit(2) on failure, and _plan_layers raises ImportError. A broken or partial scripts/ copy then kills the child mid-version.
implementation_impact: An environment fault becomes an input error. The child exits 2 after a real boot and drive, ps-run-layer appends nothing for that version, and queued versions get 'input-error after <ver>'. The run exits 2 and the E2E loop ends for the session. With ImportError, the version is recorded as crash, and a real Chromium fail may be lost.
suggestion: Require the child to load _plan_layers() eagerly in main(), before progress_init and job registration, when --sequential-browsers is given (or always in history mode). A broken sibling then becomes a true pre-run exit 2 with no boot. Add a test that patches the loader to fail and asserts no bring-up phase.

location: Boundaries > Always (Fail-fast / Slots) + I/O & Edge-Case Matrix (no skipped-child row)
issue: The spec defines which reaped children stop admission (an appended fail, exit 2, an append error), but it says nothing about a child that reports status: skipped (Playwright absent). Today such a child does not stop admission. Under slots, the remaining queued versions keep waiting and spawn children that will skip too, or they time out into no-slots. The contract output rule then prints 'skipped' with the skipped child's reason and exits 0, so any no-slots records appended in the same run never show in the output line.
implementation_impact: Implementers can reasonably choose either 'keep admitting' or 'stop like fail-fast', and the tests will not detect the difference. In the first case the operator is told 'Playwright absent', while the history silently gains no-slots records that the next plan reports as inconclusive. That can start a misdirected infra retry.
suggestion: State explicitly that a skipped child does not stop admission (unchanged from today) and that no not-run record follows it. Add an I/O row for 'first child skipped, second blocked by foreign slots until timeout' with the expected output line (skipped, exit 0), the appended list and the records, so the behaviour is pinned.

location: Tasks > docs (interim-orchestration step 3 / run-phases Fase 1/2 commands) vs Design Notes > Admission ('the queue is --cells/--versions written order')
issue: Which versions fail-fast skips, and so whether it saves any time, now depends on the order of the --cells tokens. The docs task changes the orchestrator's E2E command (drops --jobs) but never says what order the orchestrator should write the due versions in. The interim step 3 only says 'group the scoped e2e entries'.
implementation_impact: The orchestrator can put 1.7.8 first (configured or numeric ascending order), while the newest version, which SPEC names as the cheapest predictor (canary 9.1 × Chromium), runs last. When slots are short, fail-fast then skips the most informative cells, and run-to-run results depend on an unspecified ordering.
suggestion: In the interim step 3 and run-phases.md, fix the --cells order: newest version first (numeric order, descending), matching the SPEC's canary default. Alternatively, ps-run-layer can document and apply that order itself in --versions mode.

location: Boundaries > Always > Child ('with more than one engine the child logs the fallback once on stderr')
issue: In the contract, the sequential-fallback log line reports a condition: too few slots for parallel browsers (Parallel browsers > Slots). This slice passes --sequential-browsers to every child unconditionally (Design Notes > Interim cost/mode). So every multi-browser version of every run logs a 'fallback' even on an idle daemon with all 6 slots free, and the spec does not set the message text.
implementation_impact: Operators reading stderr are told on every run that slots were short. They may lower other sessions' work or raise psm_e2e_slots for no reason, and they lose the meaning of the message once CAP-7 makes it conditional again.
suggestion: Specify the CAP-3 wording so it does not claim slot shortage, for example 'browsers driven one after another (parallel browsers not implemented yet; engine fail-fast applies)'. Reserve the slot-shortage wording for CAP-7. Alternatively, log the reason that applies: 'interim: always sequential'.

location: Boundaries > Always > Child ('--run-id ... set as fl.RUN_ID before progress, job registration or labels') vs ps-plan-layers' separate ps-flashlight-run copy
issue: ps-e2e-run loads ps-flashlight-run as its own module object (fl). ps-plan-layers, which the child loads for cell_state, calls load_sibling and so execs a second, independent copy with its own random RUN_ID, _JOB, _PROGRESS and _TIMING. The spec sets --run-id only on the child's fl, and it does not say that nothing reachable through the second copy may emit progress lines or labels, or consult RUN_ID.
implementation_impact: Today derive_state touches no fl state, so this is latent. Any future helper reached through the plan-layers copy (a progress line, a label, a timing record) would carry a RUN_ID that matches no claim and no psm.run label. Claim suppression, cleanup ownership and the run_id/boot_id stamping would then silently disagree.
suggestion: State that the child uses exactly one ps-flashlight-run instance. Either make ps-e2e-run reuse plan-layers' fl (as ps-run-layer does through plan_layers().fl), or copy RUN_ID into the second instance right after loading. Add a test asserting that every flashlight module object in the child process has RUN_ID equal to --run-id.
